title: Historical orders still missing after backfill

symptom.message: Ticket: Orders that were backfilled into Snowflake last night for 3/15–3/20 still don't show up in fct_orders_daily for those dates. Ops confirmed the raw landing table has the rows. Can you find why the mart is stale?

dag.notation:
source('landing','orders_snapshot') → stg_orders_snapshot
stg_orders_snapshot → int_orders_incremental (incremental)
int_orders_incremental → fct_orders_daily

files.content:
name: debug_project
version: "1.0.0"
config-version: 2
profile: debug_project
model-paths: ["models"]
macro-paths: ["macros"]
models:
  debug_project:
    staging:
      +materialized: view
    intermediate:
      +materialized: incremental
      +unique_key: order_id
    marts:
      +materialized: table

version: 2
sources:
  - name: landing
    schema: landing
    tables:
      - name: orders_snapshot

select
    order_id,
    order_date,
    amount,
    ingested_at
from {{ source('landing', 'orders_snapshot') }}

select
    order_date,
    sum(amount) as daily_amount,
    count(*) as order_count
from {{ ref('int_orders_incremental') }}
group by 1

run_history.summary: Incremental model int_orders_incremental ran successfully; 12 rows inserted on first backfill day; subsequent run inserted 0 rows.
warnings: Adapter: incremental merge strategy — duplicates prevented by unique_key order_id

ground_truth.root_cause: Incremental predicate on int_orders_incremental uses ingested_at > max(ingested_at) from the incremental table. Late-arriving/backfilled historical rows can carry ingested_at values less than or equal to the current max ingested_at in the table, so they are skipped and never loaded.
ground_truth.fix: Replace ingestion-only incremental filter with a business-timestamp strategy (e.g. order_date window / merge on order_id with full-refresh for affected dates) or use delete+insert for impacted partitions; avoid pure max(ingested_at) predicates when backfills reuse older ingested_at.
common_misdiagnoses: Raw landing table missing rows (rows exist per ticket).
fct_orders_daily group by bug (mart reads from incomplete incremental table).
Unique key collision causing silent merge drop (wrong — rows never inserted).
investigation_path: Verify row presence in stg_orders_snapshot for missing order_date.
Compare counts in stg vs int for the same filter on order_date.
Read incremental where clause and evaluate max(ingested_at) relative to backfill rows' ingested_at.

pass_criteria: Identifies incremental where ingested_at > max(ingested_at) as the skip condition.
Explains why backfilled rows with older ingested_at are excluded.
Names int_orders_incremental as the primary failure point.

hypothesis_space.hypothesis: Incremental model unique_key is dropping duplicates incorrectly.
ingested_at incremental predicate excludes late-arriving rows with old ingestion timestamps.
fct_orders_daily date timezone shift hides weekends.

red_herrings.description: fct_orders_daily is the visible broken mart.
red_herrings.why_wrong: It aggregates whatever int_orders_incremental contains; the filter bug lives upstream in the incremental model.
